rejected.title: Different perspectives in science
card: A perspective is the way a person sees a problem. It comes from their skills, their experience and their worldview, which is how they understand the world.
Scientists often work in teams. A team with different skills, such as a biologist, an engineer and a data analyst, can notice parts of a problem that one person might miss.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples hold knowledge built up over a very long time by watching Country closely. Seasonal calendars are one example. They use signs such as flowering plants and animal behaviour to mark changes in the year.

Bringing this knowledge together with other scientific work can help a team see a problem more fully. For example, a calendar can show when plants and animals change through the year, which can help people plan when to look after land.
rejected.remember: Different skills and worldviews let a team see more of a problem.

a.q: Why can a science team with different skills and worldviews be useful?
opts: Its members can notice different parts of a problem
Its members will always reach the same conclusion
Its members no longer need to collect any evidence
Its members can finish the work without any testing
a.why: People with different skills and worldviews look at a problem in different ways, so the team can see more of it. A team does not always agree, and it still needs evidence.
a.clue: Think about what different people might notice.

b.q: A council wants to manage a river catchment in Victoria. It asks local Aboriginal Elders to share a seasonal calendar with its scientists. How could this help?
opts: It can show when plants and animals change through the year
It can replace the need to look at any other information
It can prove that no other ideas about the river matter
It can give the council exact rainfall figures for each day
b.why: A seasonal calendar records signs of change across the year, such as flowering and animal behaviour, which adds to what the scientists know. It does not replace other information, and a calendar of seasonal signs is not a record of daily rainfall.
b.clue: Think about what a seasonal calendar records.

version.title: Different perspectives in science
card: A worldview is the way a person understands the world, shaped by their culture, beliefs and experience. A person's skills and worldview both affect which parts of a problem they notice.
A team that brings together different skills and worldviews can see a problem more fully. Each member may notice evidence or questions that the others miss.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples hold knowledge of Country built over many generations of close observation. Seasonal calendars are one example: they mark seasons by signs such as plants flowering and animals breeding, not by set dates.

Many seasonal calendars have more than four seasons, each fitted to local Country. Working with Traditional Owners, who decide what knowledge to share, scientists can learn when local changes are likely to happen.
version.remember: Bringing together different skills and worldviews, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander knowledge, helps a team see more of a problem.

a.q: Team A has a biologist, a water engineer and a Traditional Owner. Team B has three biologists. Why might Team A understand a wetland's problems more fully?
opts: Its members notice things the others may miss
Its members will collect a larger amount of data
Its members will agree with each other more quickly
Its members can skip the testing of their ideas
a.why: People with different skills and worldviews notice different evidence and questions, so together they see more of the problem. Both teams have three people, so Team A will not simply collect more data.
a.clue: Both teams are the same size. What else is different?

b.q: Local Traditional Owners share part of their seasonal calendar with river scientists. It links the start of a fish's breeding to the flowering of a certain tree. How can this help the scientists?
opts: It gives a local sign that breeding is about to start
It gives the exact date that breeding starts each year
It shows the fish breed at the same time everywhere
It proves the tree flowering causes the fish to breed
b.why: A seasonal calendar marks seasons by signs in nature, so the flowering tells the scientists when breeding is likely to begin in that place. It is not a set date, and two things that happen together do not prove one causes the other.
b.clue: Is a seasonal calendar built on dates, or on what happens in nature?

a.best: Its members notice things the others may miss

b.best: It gives a local sign that breeding is about to start
